sections.h2: Contacting the Jasper County Recorder of Deeds
sections.html:
The phone is 417-358-0431 and the email is recorder@jaspercounty.org. Send mail to Post Office Box 387, Carthage, MO 64836. Recording hours run from 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Central on weekdays, closing for county holidays. That is half an hour earlier than the 4:30 p.m. close at the Carthage and Joplin county buildings, so do not count on the later time.

County offices in Carthage use 302 South Main Street, and Joplin has a county courts building at 633 South Pearl Avenue. Only the Carthage post office box is given for recording, so send deeds there, or phone before you travel anywhere in person.

sections.h2: What the recorder does in a home sale
sections.html:
This office holds the county's public land record. A deed to your buyer, a lender's release once your loan is paid, and a lien notice all take effect against the world when they are recorded here.

Inherited property works the same way: any court paper that moves title gets recorded in this office, and a future buyer's title search will read it. When your deed is filed, ask the title agent for the book and page or the document number, and keep that with your closing papers.

Go to jaspermo.icounty.com and log in with the username guest. Guests can search the index. Seeing and printing the document images takes a subscription, priced at $200 per month, or you can ask the recorder for copies.

  1. Open jaspermo.icounty.com.
  2. Type guest as the username.
  3. Search by name or by document details.
  4. Get images through a subscription or from the office.

The same system includes a fraud alert tool. Sign in, click your user name, open the iRecordWeb Notification Service Settings and enter the criteria you want watched. The email on your account then gets a message whenever a matching document is recorded.

Since August 28, 2026, a flat $2.00 statutory increase applies statewide to recording documents, marriage licenses and land surveys or plats. Senate Bill 938 created the change, and the Recorders Association of Missouri and each county recorder put it into effect. Anything recorded now carries the higher amount.

sections.h2: Does every Joplin address record here?
sections.html:
No. A small part of Joplin sits in Newton County, and parcels there are recorded with the Newton County recorder. Look at the county named on your tax statement or deed before you send anything to Carthage.

All of the other Jasper County cities record here: Carthage, Webb City, Carl Junction, Oronogo, Sarcoxie, Purcell, Neck City, Duenweg, Asbury, Alba and Reeds. If you own land near the edge of the county, check which side of the line your legal description falls on, since Newton, Lawrence, Dade and Barton counties all adjoin it.

sections.h2: Missouri fee and format rules for deeds
sections.html:
Under section 59.310 of the Missouri statutes, a recorder charges $5 for the first page of a deed and $3 for each page after that, with extra charges for copies, certificates and plats. The same section sets format rules, and a recorder can turn away a document that breaks them.

  • One-sided pages that are not bound together, in dark ink, with letters no smaller than eight-point.
  • White or pale paper, twenty-pound stock or heavier.
  • A blank three inches across the top of page one, and margins of three-quarters of an inch or more elsewhere.
  • The signer's name printed under every signature.

Copies of recorded instruments cost at most two dollars for the first page and one dollar for each later page, except plats and surveys. A certificate and seal is one dollar when it is not part of a recording. A nonconforming document can still be recorded for an added $25. Papers signed before 2002, military separation papers and certified copies are exempt from the format rules.

sections.h2: What page one of a deed must show
sections.html:
Under that blank top margin, the first page has to carry the document's title and date, each grantor with marital status, each grantee, any statutory addresses and the legal description of the land. When space runs short, say which page carries the rest. Add reference book and page numbers there too when the statute calls for them.

If the office rejects a deed, it returns the paper along with its reasons. Before you sign, compare your legal description to the one in the prior deed in the online index. A mismatch between old and new wording is the kind of problem a title agent will flag anyway.

sections.h2: Other county offices in a sale
sections.html:
Jasper County divides its work among separately elected officers, and three of them touch most house sales. Each has its own phone line.

  • Recorder of Deeds: deeds, releases and liens, 417-358-0431.
  • Collector: tax statements and payment, 417-358-0411 for real property in Carthage or 417-625-4324 in Joplin.
  • Assessor: parcel values and mailing addresses, 417-358-0440.

After a sale, ask the Assessor and the Collector whether they need the new owner's mailing address so the next tax statement reaches the right person.

Recording is only half of a clean transfer; the tax bill is the rest. The Collector, at jaspercountycollector.com, mails statements in early November that are due on receipt and delinquent after December 31. Our Jasper County property tax guide covers the offices, payment methods and dates. Once the deed is recorded, ask the Assessor to update the owner's mailing address. If a lender or the county has recorded a lien notice against your house, plan to clear it before closing, because a buyer's title search will find it in this same index.

If you are selling for cash, the same steps apply: the title company still records the deed here, pays off any lien that was recorded against the house and settles the tax. A cash sale skips the buyer's lender, so there is usually no new deed of trust to record behind yours.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Jasper County, Missouri?
faqs.a: With the Recorder of Deeds at P.O. Box 387, Carthage, MO 64836, phone 417-358-0431. Hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday.

faqs.q: How much does the Jasper County recorder charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The office quotes page-by-page prices on request. A flat $2.00 statutory increase has applied since August 28, 2026 under Missouri SB 938. Call 417-358-0431 for the exact total on your deed.

faqs.q: Can I search Jasper County land records from home?
faqs.a: Yes. Log in at jaspermo.icounty.com as guest to search the index. Viewing and printing images takes a $200 per month subscription, or you can ask the recorder for copies.

faqs.q: What happens if my deed breaks the formatting rules?
faqs.a: The recorder can send it back with an explanation, or record it for an extra $25 under Missouri statute 59.310. Fix the margins, type size and first-page details before you submit.

faqs.q: How do I get alerts if someone records a document against my property?
faqs.a: Sign in at jaspermo.icounty.com, open iRecordWeb Notification Service Settings from your user name, and add your name or parcel as criteria. The email on the account is notified of each matching recording.
